byteOpacityConstruction.octetIdentityPropertyQuotedFromControlPr: The data-plane pass-through is an OCTET-SEQUENCE IDENTITY: the octet sequence the component emits on fd1 is exactly the octet sequence the owning provider contract's host-side participant receives - equal length, equal bytes, equal order - and symmetrically for fd0 in the host-to-component direction. No insertion, deletion, substitution, reordering, or duplication of octets. The identity is stated over the octet sequence ONLY, because that is all this transport can carry: fd0/fd1 are POSIX pipes, byte streams that preserve no write boundaries, so no obligation over carrier write boundaries is enforceable here and none is stated. Both existing majors frame IN-BAND (length-delimited canonical CBOR, self-delimiting), so the enforceable frame-level obligation lives at the framing layer: after boundary recovery under the owning contract's own framing, the recovered frames must be byte-for-byte equal in equal order (judged exactly so by CC-1, CC-2, CC-9). A future subprotocol whose framing depends on carrier write boundaries cannot lawfully be carried on this transport at all: admitting one requires an explicit successor that changes the transport, and no clause of this contract may be read as promising boundary preservation the pipe does not provide.
byteOpacityConstruction.byteOpacityQuotedFromV7: Provider semantic frames are compared byte-for-byte. The control plane may decide supervision/fate only under the owning contract.
